details:
VAFEX Aerospace — Mars Reconnaissance Mission Simulator

VAFEX Aerospace is an interactive educational space exploration simulator developed to help students understand how reconnaissance orbiters operate around Mars.

Our Mission

Our objective was to create an immersive experience where players take control of a Mars reconnaissance orbiter, rather than simply watching a spacecraft animation. Players observe the planet through a simulated onboard camera, manage spacecraft resources, perform orbital maneuvers, and investigate regions that may be scientifically interesting.

How It Works

The simulation consists of three stages:

  1. Mission Launch: Players begin their Mars exploration mission.
  2. Spacecraft Configuration: Players select scientific instruments, propulsion systems, and power components while considering engineering constraints.
  3. Orbital Operations: Players enter a virtual cockpit with an interactive Mars camera, live telemetry, navigation controls, resource monitoring, and scientific instruments.

During orbital operations, players can change camera views, adjust their observation direction, target regions, and collect simulated radar observations.

Scientific Investigation

VAFEX includes three educational reconnaissance targets:

  • Arcadia Planitia
  • Utopia Planitia
  • Syrtis Major

Players investigate these regions using fictional radar observations designed to demonstrate how orbital science missions can search for possible subsurface water ice.

The simulator uses simplified orbital physics to calculate spacecraft velocity, altitude, and orbital period. Mission performance is evaluated through scientific objectives, spacecraft resources, and completed operations.

Technologies and Development

VAFEX was developed as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebGL-based visualization.

AI-assisted tools supported software development, interface design, visual assets, testing, and documentation. The project was developed as an educational prototype, not a scientifically validated spacecraft simulation. All radar findings are synthetic training data and do not represent actual discoveries.

Our Vision

We believe space exploration becomes more accessible when students can interact with scientific concepts rather than only read about them.

VAFEX combines engineering, planetary science, and interactive learning to give users a glimpse into the challenges of operating a real reconnaissance mission.

Our long-term vision is to expand VAFEX into a more detailed planetary exploration platform with improved terrain visualization, additional scientific instruments, and increasingly realistic spacecraft operations.
